html:
SMTO-EXE-0010 — SMTO couldn't safely run this administrator command

GUID: 6f5b5017-de15-4c55-8dd6-04d5cd460095
Slug: unsupported-sudo-semantics
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • The command asked for administrator (sudo) rights in a form SMTO can't check safely, such as sudo tucked inside a longer command. It was refused before running, so nothing changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to run the part that needs administrator rights as a separate command that starts with sudo. SMTO only accepts sudo at the very start of a simple command, so commands that mix it in are refused.
  2. If a whole script needs administrator rights, ask SMTO to run the entire script that way instead of just parts of it. Running a whole script as administrator is a form SMTO supports; sudo buried inside a script is not.
  3. Don't ask for commands that run as a different user account through sudo (for example sudo -u). Running as another user through sudo isn't supported, so that request will be refused again.

What success looks like

  • The command runs and shows its output in the task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Only give your administrator password when SMTO asks for it during the task, never in other messages.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Sudo normalization rejected the command because it could not prove a single leading root sudo of a literal executable or an explicit sudo <shell> -c script (nested or wrapped sudo, sudo options, alternate user, or unsupported SSH elevation).

What this means

  • Conservative sudo normalization could not prove a supported direct command or explicit root-shell payload, found nested/wrapped elevation, or rejected remote SSH elevation structure. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Conservative sudo normalization could not prove a supported direct command or explicit root-shell payload, found nested/wrapped elevation, or rejected remote SSH elevation structure.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the submitted shell structure, sudo options and any remote SSH payload; keep separate elevation scopes in separate calls.

How to fix it

  • Rewrite as sudo <executable> <args> without sudo options, or sudo sh -c '...' when the whole script or pipeline needs root; run mixed-elevation steps as separate shell.command calls, and supply sudo_password only through the credential flow. Alternate-user sudo is unsupported. The check is governed by Gate sudo (Settings › Security › Security); leave it on unless you deliberately want sudo passed through unchecked.
  • Use sudo in shell.command, or sudo sh -c '...' when the entire script needs root. Alternate-user sudo is unsupported. Supply a known sudo_password; ask_user for a missing or corrected password only after an authentication failure.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended elevation scope validates and reaches the supported private credential flow.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
